title: Etale atlas equalizer for module direct image on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism from an affine scheme $U$. Put $R=U\times_XU$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] with projections $p_1,p_2:R\to U$, and let $a=f\circ p:U\to Y$ and $b=a\circ p_1=a\circ p_2:R\to Y$. For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ on the small etale site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], write $F_U=p^*F$ and $F_R=p_1^*F_U$ (identified with $p_2^*F_U$ by the canonical fibre-product identification). Then the canonical map $f_*F\to a_*F_U$ identifies $f_*F$ with the kernel of the difference of the two restriction maps $a_*F_U\rightrightarrows b_*F_R$ induced by $p_1$ and $p_2$; equivalently, $0\to f_*F\to a_*F_U\rightrightarrows b_*F_R$ is exact at the first two terms in the category of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), proof and displayed exact sequence; the two maps are the restrictions along the projections U \times_X U \rightrightarrows U.

proof.text: For each etale scheme $V\to Y$, put $W_V=V\times_YX$, $Z_V=V\times_YU$ and $Q_V=V\times_YR$. By [lem-trf-space-atlas-base-change-cech-geometry], these are enlarged-site objects and $c_V:Z_V\to W_V$ is a singleton covering. A test map $V'\to V$ induces the three fibre-product maps, giving functors $W,Z,Q$ and a natural transformation $c:Z\to W$. The lemma identifies $Q_V\simeq Z_V\times_{W_V}Z_V$ with both projections, naturally in $V$; thus this is the overlap functor of the kernel lemma below. It also supplies the scheme $R$ and its etale projections.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), covering and overlap sentences of the proof; the overlap base is W = V times_Y X, correcting the printed subscript X.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections] to $(f,F),(a,F_U),(b,F_R)$: all three specified chart limits have small vertices in the fixed module universe and their projections are restrictions. The coefficient and source-arrow comparisons of [lem-trf-space-atlas-direct-image-section-diagram] give $\alpha_W:(f_*F)(V)\simeq\widetilde F(W_V)$, $\alpha_Z:(a_*F_U)(V)\simeq\widetilde F(Z_V)$ and $\alpha_Q:(b_*F_R)(V)\simeq\widetilde F(Q_V)$, linear and natural in $V,F$. Pullback of regular functions gives $\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X(W_V)$; restrictions give the other scalar actions. Thus the three evaluated presheaves are module sheaves. For the specified atlas arrows $\iota,r_1,r_2$ and restrictions $\rho,d_1,d_2$, these chart-preserving comparisons satisfy $\alpha_Z\iota=\rho\alpha_W$ and $\alpha_Qr_j=d_j\alpha_Z$ for $j=1,2$.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), extension to X_spaces,etale and identification of the three section terms and restriction arrows.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-enlarged-cover-module-kernel] with $M=\widetilde F$, the cover and overlap functors of step 1, and the scalar maps and sheaf conditions of step 2, in the fixed small-site universe. The equations of step 2 give $\alpha_Q((r_1-r_2)z)=(d_1-d_2)(\alpha_Zz)$. The kernel lemma gives $(d_1-d_2)\rho=0$; the equations of step 2 and injectivity of $\alpha_Q$ therefore give $(r_1-r_2)\iota=0$. Since $\alpha_Q$ is injective, $z$ is a kernel section exactly when $\alpha_Zz$ is a matching section. The cited lemma gives its unique antecedent $t$ with $\rho(t)=\alpha_Zz$; define $\beta(z)=\alpha_W^{-1}(t)$. Then $\alpha_Z(\iota\beta(z))=\rho(t)=\alpha_Zz$, so $\iota\beta(z)=z$. For $s\in(f_*F)(V)$, uniqueness identifies the antecedent of $\alpha_Z\iota(s)=\rho\alpha_W(s)$ with $\alpha_W(s)$, giving $\beta\iota(s)=s$. The inverse is linear by the lemma and step 2. Moreover, $\alpha_Z\iota=\rho\alpha_W$ and injectivity of $\rho,\alpha_W$ show that $\iota$ is injective. For $h:V'\to V$, naturality of $\iota$ gives $\iota_{V'}(\beta_V(z)|_{V'})=z|_{V'}=\iota_{V'}\beta_{V'}(z|_{V'})$; injectivity of $\iota_{V'}$ proves that $\beta$ commutes with restriction. For $m:F\to G$, both $(f_*m)\beta_F(z)$ and $\beta_G((a_*p^*m)z)$ map to $(a_*p^*m)z$ under $\iota_G$, so injectivity gives their equality. Thus these linear inverses form the required natural isomorphism of module sheaves for the specified atlas arrow, with exactness at the first two terms.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), sheaf-condition paragraph and final functoriality sentence, extracted as a statement for a functorial family of covers with compatible scalar actions.
